This introduction section from a 2025 BJ article by Malak Haidar outlines the significance of Theileria annulata as a protozoan parasite and its effects on host leukocyte transformation and health implications in cattle.

Theileria annulata is an intracellular protozoan and a member of the phylum Apicomplexa . T. annulata, a tick-borne hemoparasite [1] , causes leukoproliferative diseases [2] in cattle, commonly known as tropical theileriosis. Theileria parasites have significant impacts on both animal and human welfare. Uniquely, they can transform their host cells by profoundly hijacking their signaling cascades [3] , leading to cancer-like phenotype characterized by immortalization, hyper-proliferation, and aggressive dissemination. However, dissemination can be attenuated by multiple in vitro passages [4] . Theileria parasites are recognized as master manipulators of their host cells, as reviewed in [5] . They modify host gene expression through both post-transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms to support their development [6] .

metadata.title: Defining epitranscriptomic hallmarks at the host-parasite interface and their roles in virulence and disease progression in Theileria annulata -infected leukocytes.
metadata.abstract: Theileria parasites are known to induce the transformation of host bovine leukocytes, involved in rapid proliferation, evasion from apoptotic mechanisms, and increased dissemination. In this study, we reveal the involvement of m 6 A RNA modification in T. annulata infection-induced transformation of bovine leukocytes. We conducted m 6 A sequencing and bioinformatics analysis to map the mRNA methylation patterns of T. annulata -infected host leukocytes. We observe specific mRNA modifications for T. annulata -infected leukocytes and a strong correlation between the proliferation rate of the infected Leukocytes with m 6 A modifications We observe that the increased amounts of m 6 A seem to impact some cell cycle dynamics, potentially via modifications of E2F4 mRNA. Moreover, we further identify HIF-1α as a possible driver of these m 6 A RNA modifications that have clear relevance to cellular proliferation dynamics. Overall, our results provide insights into the role of m6A mRNA methylation in the molecular crosstalk between Theileria and their host leukocytes, emphasizing the critical role of mRNA methylation in host-parasite interaction.

This introduction section from Malak Haidar's article discusses the role of m6A methyltransferase complexes, particularly METTL3 and METTL14, in the regulation of m6A modifications in mRNA and their potential biological functions.

Intriguingly, m 6 A peaks can aggregate in distinct regions, serving various biological functions [25] . m 6 A methyltransferase complexes oversee all m 6 A mRNA modifications. Central to the complex is a heterodimer comprising two writer-proteins: METTL3 and METTL14. METTL3 is the catalytic core, while METTL14 provides structural support. WTAP (Wilms' Tumor 1-Associating Protein) stabilizes this core. RNA-Binding Motif protein 15 (RBM15) assists in guiding the complex to its targets. Conversely, "erasers" such as the fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) and alkB homolog 5 (ALKBH5) function as demethylases, removing m 6 A marks. Several m6A-binding proteins, including YTHDF1–3 and YTHDC1, are identified as m 6 A "readers" [26-29] . YTH domain family proteins might interact with unique subsets of m6A sites, leading to diverse gene expression outcomes [30] .

processed_chunks.text:
This Results section from Malak Haidar's article investigates how m6A modification influences the proliferation of Theileria-infected leukocytes by analyzing specific bovine mRNAs associated with G2 and G2/M phase modulation.

S1)). Acknowledging that host cell proliferation is pivotal in Theileria -mediated pathogenesis [44] , we sifted through our Me-RIP dataset to identify m6A-modified bovine mRNAs transcribed by genes integral to G2 and G2/M phase modulation such as CDC2, CDK1, CCNB1, CCNB2, BUB1, BUB1B, and CDC25B,Cyclin B1,E2F4 [45, 46] . Among these, only the E2F transcription factor family member (E2F4) bore m6A modifications. Earlier research affirmed that E2F4 partly functions as a transcriptional catalyst, regulating the expression of cell cycle-associated genes [47] . Notably, our meRIP-seq dataset revealed heightened levels of methylated E2F4 mRNA relative to its non-methylated counterpart. To validate the hypothesis that m6A modification modulates E2F4 expression, we quantified E2F4 mRNA levels post METTL3 overexpression in virulent macrophages. E2F4 expression heightens in conjunction with rising m6A levels ( Figure.4C , right). For more confirmation, we looked for genes known to be regulated by E2F4 in bovine cells [48, 49] , but we could only identify four genes: SIRT5, mTOR, SREBP‐1c (gene is SREBF1), and Cyclin D1 (gene is CCND1). We indicated SIRT5, mTOR, and SREBP‐1c on a volcano plot (Fig. S2). None of these genes show significant differential gene expression (DGE), but they are all downregulated in Vm compared to V. We then examined a ChIP-Seq study from humans [50] . This study identified 16,246 peaks (putative E2F4 binding sites) in the hg18 genome. Using this annotation, we found that 4,739 human genes have peaks within their 250 bp upstream region. Of these, we identified 3,960 corresponding bovine genes in our RNA DEseq output. Upon examining these bovine genes, where the human version has an upstream putative E2F4 binding site, we observed that 43 are upregulated and 114 are downregulated. Over 72% of these DGE genes are downregulated (corresponding to the repressor activity of E2F4) compared to the rest of the DGE genes, of which only approximately 35% are downregulated. This finding is highly significant (attached, bottom plot) and suggests that genes potentially regulated by E2F4 are downregulated in Vm (Fig. S2). Collectively, these findings reinforce the notion that m6A modulates cell cycle dynamics via E2F4 mRNA modifications.

Collectively, these findings reinforce the notion that m6A modulates cell cycle dynamics via E2F4 mRNA modifications. ### HIF-1α-promotes proliferation of Theileria -infected leukocytes by inducing m6A-RNA methylation

HIF-1α levels are significantly higher in attenuated macrophages than in their virulent counterparts, even after losing their tumorigenic phenotype [51] . Pharmacological inhibition of HIF-1α is found to prevent the proliferation of Theileria -infected macrophages [51] . Additionally, HIF-1α inhibition in T. annulata -infected B cells abolishes their ability to form colonies in soft agar, most likely due to growth arrest [52] . Importantly, HIF-1α has been shown to enhance the expression of WTAP leading to a change in m 6 A distribution and boosting cell proliferation in acute myeloid leukemia [53] . HIF-1α also directly binds to the promoter region of YTHDF1, regulating its transcription under hypoxic conditions in hepatocellular carcinoma [54] .

The impact of pathogens on host epigenetics offers invaluable insights into the complex interactions that underlie infection and disease progression. Among these, Theileria parasites, specifically transforming species such as T. annulata , excel at altering host cellular behavior. This capability is evident in pathological outcomes such as unchecked cellular proliferation and an increased resistance to apoptosis. Recent research has enriched our comprehension of the ways Theileria parasites reshape the transcriptomes of infected cells. Yet, the exploration of the epigenetic dimension — particularly T. annulata 's impact on mRNA methylation — remains a yet-to-be-unfolded area of study.
